a substantial number of HIV-infected patients still take two NRTIs, that the great majority of these patients have a stable disease and that the shift to a three antiretrovials regimen is expected to lead long-term advantages in the majority of patients.

a significant proportion of HIV-infected patients treated with HAART still take a dual nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor combination and that the great majority of these patients have a stable disease evolution.
a significant proportion of patients with HIV infection are still treated with a dual NRTIs combination, and that this approach seems to be associated with a stable disease course.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the outcomes of dual NRTI therapy in the HAART period and the long-term evolution of the disease in a large population of HIV-infected patients treated at a single university hospital in the north of Italy.

the frequency, background, and long-term evolution (at least 24 months) of anti-HIV treatments conducted with two nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) in a population of 798 HIV-infested patients in a single university hospital.
the outcomes of dual NRTI therapy in the HAART period.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dual nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors treatment is still used, in the HAART period, as a safe and effective option, particularly in the case of a low risk of HIV disease progression.
dual NRTI combinations may have residual indications, and may be safely used for long-term periods, in a selected group of HIV-infected patients with a low disease progression risk.

the dual NRTI approach is still a valid therapeutic choice in a significant proportion of HIV-infected patients, especially in the case of low viral load, low CD4(+) cell count and/or previous antiretrovural failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of patients on dual nucleoside therapy have a stable course of disease, but there may be a subset of patients who would benefit from a triple therapy.
dual NRTI combinations can provide effective and safe antiretrovirus therapy in the era of HAART, especially when the baseline CD4(+) cell count is above 350 cells/mu L.

, in the HAART-era, dual nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor therapy may have residual indications and may be safely continued in patients who have a good virological response and a stable immunological course.
The main takeaway from our work is that

dual NRTI therapy is still used in a considerable proportion of HIV-infected patients, and that it can lead to a stable disease course, even in the presence of a high HIV load or a low CD4(+) count at baseline.
, in the HAART-era, a substantial proportion of HIV-infected patients are still treated with a dual NRTIs, and the great major of these patients have a stable disease progression.

dual NRTI antiretrovirus therapy may be considered a safe and effective treatment option for patients with a low viral load and high CD4(+) cell count, who do not need to be treated with protease inhibitors or nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors.
